en: The Compendium of the Buddha’s Past Deeds, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty.
Chapter One: The Resolve to Offer Worship. Chapter One: The Resolve to Offer Worship.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana, the Ocean of Great Wisdom. Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the Kalandaka Bamboo Grove at Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus.

At that time, the Tathāgata dwelt in the conduct of a Buddha, free from all further afflictions; therefore he was named Jina. He had attained all-knowledge, practiced all-knowledge, and realized all-knowledge. He dwelt in celestial conduct, dwelt in Brahma-conduct, and dwelt in noble conduct, having attained mastery over his mind.

Relying upon the various World-Honored Ones, they desire to practice all manner of deeds and are able to accomplish them all; they receive great offerings, honor, and respect from the fourfold assembly of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, as well as from kings, ministers, prime ministers, various non-Buddhists, and śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas alike.

The Buddha obtained such various offerings—food, drink, clothing, bedding, and medicine—wherein these four requisites were fully provided and entirely complete; they were most excellent and most sublime, with nothing equal to them.
Foremost in wisdom, his fame is heard afar; though he receives offerings and sustenance, his mind remains untainted, just as a lotus flower is not defiled by water.
The World-Honored One’s name, his teaching, and the sound of his voice are the most supreme and excellent in the world, with none surpassing them.

Thus, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, fully endowed with these ten titles, possesses supernormal knowledge that pervades all among the present devas, Māras, Brahmās, Śakras, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and the entire world of gods and humans.

Having known [all things], he preaches the Dharma; as he moves through the world, his words—whether at the beginning, the end, or in the middle—are all excellent. His phrasing and meaning are skillful, his principles are subtle and profound, and he is adorned with the primary and secondary marks. Possessing the pure brahmacarya in its entirety without deficiency, he proclaims and elucidates it.
At that time, in the early morning, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana adjusted his robes, took up his alms bowl, and entered the city of Rājagṛha, intending to go on his almsround.
Then Maudgalyāyana stood alone and reflected:
"It is still too early for almsround this morning; I shall first proceed to the Śuddhāvāsa heavens."

Having formed this thought, the Venerable Maudgalyāyana—just as a strong man might bend or extend his arm—disappeared from Rājagṛha and, before his body was seen, suddenly stood present in the palaces of the Śuddhāvāsa devas.
At that time, the gods of the immeasurable Śuddhāvāsa heavens, seeing Maudgalyāyana approaching with composure, felt great joy in their hearts and said to one another:
"We should now go together to welcome the Venerable Maudgalyāyana."

Having spoken these words, they followed him to the place where Maudgalyāyana was, prostrated themselves at Maudgalyāyana’s feet with their heads, stood to one side, and addressed Maudgalyāyana, saying:
"Venerable Maudgalyāyana!"
Rare! Rare indeed,
Venerable Maudgalyāyana!
In this world, they are difficult to see and difficult to encounter—
namely, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha— who for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas have diligently cultivated all practices.
And he spoke in verse:
"Throughout hundreds of thousands of kalpas, Diligently seeking the path to enlightenment for a vast duration of time,
You are the great jewel among sentient beings."
"Rare in this world to behold, Is only the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
At that time, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, having heard these verses from the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven, his entire body trembled and the hair on his skin stood on end, and he thought to himself:
"How extraordinary!"
How rare! How inconceivable!

Difficult to see and difficult to encounter is the Buddha, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; he is hard to meet in the world, appearing but once in the course of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of kalpas.

At that time, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, within the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, expounded for that assembly of devas countless kinds of subtle and wondrous dharmas; he manifested the immeasurable meanings of pure dharmas and proclaimed the infinite, profound, and secret essentials of the Dharma, causing each of the devas’ hearts to give rise to joy.
Having completed his teaching and demonstration, and out of reverence for the Dharma, he vanished from that place and returned to this Jambudvīpa.

Just as a strong man might bend and then extend his arm in a single thought-moment, he arrived at Rājagṛha. He went on his alms-round in due order, returned to his original location, finished his meal, set aside his robes and bowl, washed his feet, and proceeded to where the Buddha was.
Having arrived at the place where the Buddha was, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to sit to one side, and once seated, spoke to the Buddha concerning the place from which he had come:
“World-Honored One!”
This morning, while begging for alms, I arrived at the city of Rājagṛha and proceeded to the Śuddhāvāsa heaven.
A deity there said to me:
"The Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, is difficult to encounter and difficult to meet within this world."
Having related what was previously said, he addressed the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!

Having heard such rare words as these, they are truly inconceivable—that the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas appear in the world but once in immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kalpas."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Maudgalyāyana, saying: "Maudgalyāyana!
The devas of the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens possess little knowledge and little vision; yet, with their limited and inferior wisdom, they are able to know the events of hundreds of thousands of kalpas."
Why is this so? Maudgalyāyana!
I recall that in the past, in the presence of immeasurable and boundless World-Honored Ones, I planted various roots of goodness, even unto my seeking of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Maudgalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Wheel-Turning Sage King, I encountered thirty billion Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name: Śākyamuni Tathāgata, along with their assemblies of śrāvakas. I honored, served, and reverently made offerings to them, providing the four requisites in full—namely, clothing, food and drink, bedding, and medicine for illness.

At that time, those Buddhas did not bestow upon me the prediction: "In a future age, you shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and become a Knower of the World, a Teacher of Gods and Humans, a Buddha, a World-Honored One, having realized Perfect Enlightenment."
"Maugandalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Cakravartin King, I encountered eight hundred million Buddhas, all bearing the same name: Dīpaṃkara Tathāgata, along with their assemblies of śrāvakas. I honored and revered them, making offerings of the four requisites—namely, clothing, food and drink, bedding and seats, and medicinal elixirs—as well as banners, canopies, flowers, and incense."

At that time, those Buddhas did not bestow upon me the prediction: "You shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, as well as the title of Knower of the World, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, and World-Honored One."
"Maugandalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Wheel-Turning Sage King, I encountered three hundred million Buddhas, all bearing the same name: Vipaśyin Tathāgata. Together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, I made offerings of the four requisites to them, providing everything in full abundance."
At that time, those Buddhas did not bestow upon me the prediction, as previously described, saying, "You shall become a Buddha.
Maudgalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Cakravartin King, I encountered ninety thousand Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name, Kāśyapa Tathāgata, along with their assemblies of śrāvakas. I provided them with the four types of offerings in full abundance; yet even then, they did not bestow upon me the prediction that I would attain Buddhahood, as previously described.
“Maudgalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Wheel-Turning Sage King, I encountered sixty thousand Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name: Dīpaṃkara Tathāgata. Together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, I made offerings of the four requisites to them, providing them all in full abundance. Yet, they did not grant me a prediction that I would become a Buddha, as described above.”
"Maugandalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Wheel-Turning Sage King, I personally made offerings to eighteen thousand Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name: Tathāgata Śālarāja. I provided them and their assemblies of śrāvakas with the four types of requisites, fulfilling every requirement, and only thereafter did I leave the household life."
He formed this thought:
"For the sake of future ages, I shall attain the Buddha-way and uphold the prohibitive precepts.
At that time, those Buddhas did not bestow a prediction upon him, until he became a Buddha, as described above.
"Maugandalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Cakravartin King, I personally made offerings to ten thousand Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name: Tathāgata Able to Cross to the Other Shore (Pāragāmī). Together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, I provided them with the four types of requisites in full abundance. Yet, they did not bestow upon me a prediction that I would attain Buddhahood."
“Maudgalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Cakravartin King, I personally made offerings to fifteen thousand Buddhas, all of whom shared the same title, namely Tathāgata Sun. Together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, I provided them with the four types of requisites, fully and completely. Yet, they did not bestow upon me a prophecy that I would attain Buddhahood.”
"Maugandalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Cakravartin King, I personally made offerings to two thousand Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name: Tathāgata Kauṇḍinya. Together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, I provided them with the four types of requisites, fully and completely. Yet, not even one of them bestowed upon me a prediction that I would attain Buddhahood."
"Maudgalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a universal monarch (cakravartin), I personally made offerings to six thousand Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name: Tathāgata Nāga. Together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, I provided them with the four requisites of worship, fully and completely. Yet, they did not bestow upon me a prediction (vyākaraṇa) that I would attain Buddhahood."
"Maugandalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Cakravartin King, I personally made offerings to one thousand Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name: Tathāgata Indraketu. Together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, I provided them with the four types of requisites, fully and completely. Yet, they did not bestow upon me a prediction that I would attain Buddhahood."
“Maudgalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Cakravartin King, I once made offerings to five hundred Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name: Padmottara Tathāgata. Together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, I provided them with the four types of requisites, fulfilling every need. Yet, they did not grant me a prophecy that I would attain Buddhahood.”

"Maugalyāyana! I recall that in the past, when I was a Wheel-Turning Sage King, I personally made offerings to sixty-four Buddhas, all of whom shared the same name: Tathāgata Śaṅkhakuśa. Together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, I provided them with the four types of requisites in full abundance; yet, not even one of them bestowed upon me the prediction that I would become a Buddha."
“Maudgalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, when I was a Wheel-Turning Sage King, I once made offerings to a Buddha named Samyakpratipadita Tathāgata and his assembly of śrāvakas. I provided them with all four types of requisites, fully and completely. Yet, that Buddha did not grant me a prediction that I would attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, as well as the state of vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna and sarvalokavid.”
“Maudgalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, I made offerings to eighty-eight thousand *koṭis* of *pratyekabuddhas*, providing them with banners, canopies, incense, and flowers—the four requisites in full—and even after those Buddhas had passed into *parinirvāṇa*, I erected stupas and temples for them and made offerings as before; yet they did not grant me this prediction: ‘You shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.’”
“Maudgalyāyana!
I recall that in the past there was a Tathāgata named Suvicintita, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha.”
In the presence of that Buddha, Maitreya Bodhisattva first gave rise to the aspiration for enlightenment, planted various roots of goodness, and sought anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva will become a Cakravartin Universal Monarch named Vairocana.
At that time, the lifespan of the people will be eighty thousand years.
"Maudgalyāyana!

At the first assembly when that Tathāgata Subhūṣita preached the Dharma, ninety-six trillion people attained the path of Arhatship; at the second assembly when he preached the Dharma, eighty-four trillion people attained the path of Arhatship; and at the third assembly when he preached the Dharma, seventy-two trillion people attained the path of Arhatship."
“Maudgalyāyana!

That Cakravartin King Vairocana made offerings to that Tathāgata Subhūṣita and his assembly of śrāvakas, honoring and respecting them with the four requisites complete: banners, canopies, flowers, and incense.”
"Maugandalyāyana!

At that time, the Cakravartin King Vairocana, seeing that Tathāgata endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs, as well as the assembly of śrāvakas, the adornments of the Buddha-field, and the span of his lifespan, immediately gave rise to the mind of enlightenment and spoke these words with his own mouth:
'How rare, World-Honored One!'"

"May I, in a future life, attain Buddhahood, fully endowed with the ten titles, just like the Tathāgata Sunetra of today; may I be surrounded by a great assembly of śrāvakas, devas, and humans who pay me homage, and may they listen to my preaching of the Dharma, accepting it with faith and putting it into practice, exactly as they do now, without any difference."
Maitreya spoke again:
"May I, in the future, bring about various benefits for many sentient beings, bestow peace and happiness, and have compassion for all the worlds of devas and humans."
"Maudgalyāyana!

The Bodhisattva Maitreya conceived the aspiration for enlightenment more than forty kalpas before I did; it was only after that that I first conceived the mind of the Way, planted various roots of goodness, and sought anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
“Maudgalyāyana!
I recall that in the past there was a Buddha named Śāsanadhvaja Tathāgata.
Maudgalyāyana!”

In that buddha-field, I became a wheel-turning sage king named Dṛḍhadhanu; there, I first gave rise to the mind of enlightenment, planted various roots of goodness, and sought anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, I made offerings to that Buddha, the World-Honored One, for a full thousand years, as well as to his assembly of śrāvakas; I venerated, honored, prostrated to, and praised them, providing them with the four requisites in abundance. I offered five hundred sets of exquisite garments all at once, and even after that Buddha had entered parinirvāṇa, I erected a stūpa for his relics one yojana high and half a yojana wide, adorned with the seven treasures—namely gold, silver, crystal, lapis lazuli, red pearls, and so forth—and embellished with musaragalva and agate. Furthermore, I used various banners, canopies, pennants, bells, incense, flowers, lamps, and candles to make offerings.
"Maugalyāyana!
Having made such offerings as these, I diligently applied myself day and night and made this vast vow:
'When I attain Buddhahood in the future, may there be no sentient beings who are unfilial toward their parents, nor [who...]"
They show reverence neither to śramaṇas nor to brāhmaṇas; they fail to recognize the distinctions between kin and strangers or between the honorable and the lowly within their own households.
Lacking faith and respect, they do not believe in the causes and effects of karma across the three periods of time, nor do they believe that there are holy persons existing in the present.
They practice not a single virtuous dharma, but instead indulge solely in greed, hatred, and delusion, fully committing the ten unwholesome deeds.
Having performed only mixed karma and not a single virtuous deed,
may I attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* within that world; out of compassion for all those sentient beings,

may I preach the Dharma and perform transformative teachings to bring great benefit, rescuing and protecting them, and through loving-kindness and compassion, may I deliver them so they are freed from suffering.
"Establishing all those in suffering within happiness, he extensively expounds the Dharma for those devas and humans.
"Maudgalyāyana!
Such are the rare and extraordinary deeds of asceticism performed by the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, for the sake of all sentient beings."
“Maudgalyāyana!
All bodhisattvas possess four kinds of subtle and wondrous conduct.
What are these four?
1. Practice of intrinsic nature;
2. Practice of the nature of aspiration;
3. Practice of the nature of conformity.
Fourth, the nature of transformation.
Maudgalyāyana!
What is called "action by intrinsic nature"?

If bodhisattvas, from their very nature, have been virtuous and upright, obeying the instructions of their parents; if they have faith and respect for śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas; if they well understand the distinctions of honor and intimacy within their families and, having understood them, treat them with reverence and serve them without fail; and if they are fully endowed with the ten wholesome paths of action while further extensively practicing other wholesome deeds—this is called the bodhisattva’s conduct of natural disposition (*svabhāvacaryā*).
What is called the nature of the practice of aspiration?
It is when bodhisattvas make such an aspiration:
"At what time shall I attain Buddhahood, becoming an Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, fully endowed with the ten titles?"
This is called the bodhisattva’s practice of the nature of aspiration.
What is called the practice of the nature of conformity?
It is when bodhisattvas fully accomplish and perfect the six pāramitās.
What are these six?
They are the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*); these are called the bodhisattva’s practice in accordance with nature (*anuloma-gotra-carita*).
What is meant by the practice that transforms nature (*parivṛtti-gotra-carita*)?

"Just as I made offerings to the World-Honored One Dīpaṃkara, and by virtue of those causes and conditions, I came to know through recitation— this is called the bodhisattva’s transformation of their fundamental nature and conduct,
Maudgalyāyana!"
"These are called the four kinds of natures and practices of a bodhisattva.
At that time, the World-Honored One was in Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park; having attained Buddhahood, he abided in the conduct of a Buddha, briefly explaining as above.
Then, having finished his meal, the Buddha entered meditative concentration for seven days, recollecting the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past.
At that time, after seven days had passed, Ānanda went to where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to sit to one side,
and addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One!”
How rare is the Tathāgata! His body is pure and his countenance is majestic; as I saw him before, it now appears twice as radiant as usual, with his glorious light greatly intensified.
“The faculties of the World-Honored One are immeasurably tranquil; in what samādhi do you sit, and upon what dharma-characteristics are you contemplating?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"So it is, Ānanda!

Just as you have said, when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha enters into meditative absorption and dwells there, recollecting the past Buddhas and Tathāgatas who have attained the wisdom of great sovereign supernormal powers, he may wish to remain for a kalpa or less than a kalpa; he recollects the wisdom of hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddhas, and yet the wisdom of the Tathāgata remains entirely unimpeded."
Why is this? Because the Tathāgata has attained the other shore through the possession of the wisdom of all Buddhas. Ānanda!

Once the Tathāgata has finished his single meal, he may remain for one kalpa or less than one kalpa; whether he wishes to remain for more or less time, he does so with sovereign ease, free from any fatigue.
"Why is this? Because the Tathāgata has fully attained the samādhis of all Buddhas and reached the other shore; among all samādhis, this is the most supreme.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“I recall that in the past, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there was a Buddha in the world named Śakraketu Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. He was able to serve as a place of refuge for all immeasurable sentient beings; he was able to serve as a compassionate abode for sentient beings; he was well able to pity all sentient beings and bestow peace and happiness upon them; he possessed great majestic virtue, surrounded before and behind by an immeasurable assembly of noble ones.”
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Śakradhvaja has five billion assemblies of śrāvakas, all of whom have realized the fruit of arhatship and live for five thousand years.
That Tathāgata Śakradhvaja bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Urdhvadhvaja Tathāgata. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Urdhvadhvaja, in turn, bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Dhvajaketu Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Dhvajaketu further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "He shall next become a buddha named Priyadhvaja Tathāgata. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Priyadhvaja further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying: "In the future, you shall become a Buddha named Daśadhvaja Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Daśadhvaja further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying: "In the future, you shall become a Buddha named Durjayadhvaja Tathāgata."
“Ānanda! That Tathāgata Durdharadhvaja further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Pradīpa Tathāgata. Ānanda!”
That Tathāgata Pradīpa again bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Supradīpa Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Supradīpa again bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Pratiṣṭhita Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Pratiṣṭhita further grants a prediction to another bodhisattva, saying: "In the future, you shall become a Buddha named Supratiṣṭhita. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Supratisthita further conferred a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Nāgendra Tathāgata. Ānanda!
That Nāgendra Tathāgata will in turn confer a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Anupamavikramatejas Tathāgata.
“Ānanda! That Tathāgata Anupamavikrama will further bestow a prediction upon another bodhisattva, who shall next become a buddha named Āryajanman Tathāgata. Ānanda!”
That Tathāgata, born of the noble ones, further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Suśreṣṭha.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Suśreṣṭha further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Ṛṣiśreṣṭha.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Ṛṣabha-vijaya further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "In the future, he shall become a Buddha named Samanta-chāyā Tathāgata. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Samantacchāya further bestowed a prediction upon a bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Pratyutpannanimitta Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Pratyutpannanimitta further bestowed a prediction upon a bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Uccakula Tathāgata.
"Ānanda! That Tathāgata Uttarakula further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: 'The next one to become a Buddha shall be named Svaviṣaya Tathāgata. Ānanda!"
That Tathāgata Svaviṣaya further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Asama-tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Asama-tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Krakucchanda-tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Krakucchanda further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Mahāprabha Tathāgata. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Mahāprabha further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying: "In the future, you shall become a Buddha named Vigatāśoka Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Vigatāśoka Tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying: "In the future, you shall become a Buddha named Tyaktodakaugha Tathāgata."
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Praśāntodaka further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying: "The next one to become a Buddha shall be named Mahābala Tathāgata. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Mahābala further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "The next one shall become a Buddha named Tīrṇapāra Tathāgata.
"Ānanda! That Tīrṇapāra Tathāgata will further bestow a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: 'The next one shall become a Buddha named Sūrya Tathāgata.'"
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Sun further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "The next one to become a buddha shall be named Tathāgata Śānta. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Śānta further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Mahāghoṣasvara Tathāgata. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Mahāghoṣasvara further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Svārāja Tathāgata.
“Ānanda! That Tathāgata Svārāja further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Ratnarāja Tathāgata. Ānanda!”
That Tathāgata Ratnarāja further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Sukhāvatīrāja.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Sukhāvatīrāja further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Sūkṣma.
"Ānanda! That Subtle Tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: 'The next one to become a Buddha shall be named Brahma-voice Tathāgata. Ānanda!"
That Tathāgata Brahmaghoṣa further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a Buddha named Guṇotpāda Tathāgata.

That Tathāgata Guṇotpāda will have seventy billion śrāvaka disciples, all of whom will have realized the fruit of arhatship. The lifespan of that Buddha will be a full seventy thousand years, and after his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma will remain in the world for a full three thousand years.
“Ānanda! That Tathāgata Guṇasambhava further bestows a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Nāgadṛśa Tathāgata.
Once that Nāgadṛśa Tathāgata has attained awakening, he will remain in the world for one kalpa for the sake of all sentient beings.”
“Ānanda! That Tathāgata Avalokita further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: ‘In the future, he shall become a Buddha named Abhayottara Tathāgata. Ānanda!”
That Tathāgata Abhayottama further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Nāgottama Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Nāgottama Tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Devaguṇa Tathāgata.
"Ānanda! That Tathāgata Guṇadatta further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: 'In the future, he shall become a Buddha named Śarīravarottama Tathāgata. Ānanda!"
The Tathāgata Śarīravarṣa further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Anupamendu Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Anupamendu further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Hetuśreṣṭha Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Superior had one thousand six hundred śrāvaka disciples, all of whom were arhats. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Superior Purple (Śikhin) further conferred a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "In the future, you shall become a Buddha named Tathāgata Purple Superior. "Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Purple Superior further conferred a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: 'In the future, you shall become a Buddha named Tathāgata Tagaraśikhin.'"
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Tagarasikhin further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "In the future, he shall become a Buddha named Padmottara. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Padmottara further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "The next one to become a Buddha shall be named Kauṇḍinya Tathāgata. Ānanda!
There shall be one hundred Buddhas with that same name, and the kalpa in which they dwell shall be named Lesser Lotus."
Each of those Tathāgatas Kauṇḍinya had three hundred billion śrāvaka disciples, all of whom were arhats.
Each of those Tathāgatas lived for three hundred years, and after the parinirvāṇa of each Buddha, the True Dharma remained in the world for another three hundred years.
“Ānanda! That last Tathāgata Kauṇḍinya will further bestow a prediction upon one bodhisattva, who shall next become a buddha named Candana Tathāgata. Ānanda!”
That Candana Tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "Next you shall become a buddha named Pradīpa Tathāgata.
"Ānanda! That Pradīpa Tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: 'Next you shall become a buddha named Hitaiṣin Tathāgata.'"
“Ānanda! That Tathāgata Arthadarśin further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Śubhavyūha Tathāgata.

That Śubhavyūha Tathāgata, observing all sentient beings with his Buddha-eye and desiring to have compassion for them, shall remain in the world for a thousand kalpas so as not to sever the lineage of the Buddhas.”
That Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha of Virtuous Excellence has thirty-two billion nayutas of śrāvaka disciples, all of whom are arhats.
"Ānanda! That Tathāgata Kuśala further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: 'In the future, he shall become a Buddha named Prabhūtaratna Tathāgata. Ānanda!"
That Tathāgata Uṣṇīṣa-vijaya further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "Next you shall become a Buddha named Lokapāla-santuṣṭa Tathāgata.
That Tathāgata Lokapāla-santuṣṭa will become a Buddha after the passing of immeasurable nayutas of kalpas.
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Lokapāla-saṃtuṣṭa has twenty billion śrāvaka disciples, all of whom are arhats.
"Ānanda! [he said].
That Tathāgata Lokapāla-saṃtuṣṭa further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "In the future, you shall become a Buddha named Śikhin Tathāgata. Ānanda!

At the place where that Śikhin Tathāgata attains Buddhahood, the kalpa shall be named Padma. Within that kalpa, sixty-two others, all bearing the same name Śikhin, shall successively attain Buddhahood as Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

Ānanda, that Śikhin Tathāgata, who was the very last among them to attain bodhi, further bestowed a prediction upon a bodhisattva, saying: "The next one shall become a Buddha, named Janman Tathāgata."
Ānanda! That Buddha, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, out of compassion for all sentient beings, remained in the world to teach and transform them for a full two thousand kalpas.
“Ānanda! That Tathāgata Janman will further bestow a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: ‘In the future, he shall become a Buddha named Sunetra Tathāgata. Ānanda!”
That Tathāgata Sunetra further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "The next one to become a Buddha shall be named Śreṣṭhin Tathāgata. "Ānanda!
That Śreṣṭhin Tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: 'The next one to become a Buddha shall be named Sujāta Tathāgata.'"

Ānanda! That Buddha Sujāta, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, had a short lifespan, remaining for only a single day; during that interval, he taught and transformed eighty-four thousand śrāvakas, causing them all to attain the fruit of arhatship.
"Ānanda! That Tathāgata Sujāta further conferred a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Brahmaguṇa Tathāgata. Ānanda!"
That Tathāgata Brahmaguṇa had thirty-two billion śrāvaka disciples, all of whom were arhats;
after that Tathāgata Brahmaguṇa entered parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma remained in the world for a full thirty thousand years.
“Ānanda! That Tathāgata Brahmaguṇa further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: ‘In the future, he shall become a Buddha named Utpalaguṇa Tathāgata. Ānanda!”
That Tathāgata Nīlotpala further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Sudarśana Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Buddha Sudarśana, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, will have three thousand koṭis of śrāvaka disciples, all of whom are arhats.
“Ānanda! That Tathāgata Sudarśana further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Satyadarśin Tathāgata. Ānanda!”
That Tathāgata Dṛṣṭasatya further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Mūla-tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Mūla-tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Pītavarṇa-tathāgata.
"Ānanda! That Purple Tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: 'In the future, he shall become a Buddha named Other Tathāgata. Ānanda!"
That Tathāgata, in turn, conferred a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a Buddha named Namdusuk (South Star) Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Namdusuk Tathāgata, in turn, conferred a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a Buddha named Sāla Tathāgata.
Ānanda! That Śāla Tathāgata further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying: "The next one to become a buddha shall be named Jinendra Tathāgata. Ānanda!
That Tathāgata Mahādhipati further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying: "The next shall become a Buddha named Mahādhipati Tathāgata.
"Ānanda! That Tathāgata Mahādhipati further bestowed a prediction upon one bodhisattva, saying: 'The next shall become a Buddha named Jñānavijaya Tathāgata.'"
Ānanda! That Tathāgata Jñānavijaya further bestowed a prediction upon another bodhisattva, saying that he shall next become a buddha named Samantabhadra Tathāgata.
